data.text: React Spring uses spring physics to create natural-looking animations instead of fixed durations.

data.title: React Spring

data.text: react-spring animates values toward a target using spring physics rather than a fixed duration, so motion feels natural and adapts to interruption. It also drives non-CSS values such as an SVG path length or a three-dimensional rotation through the same `useSpring` hook.

data.title: A spring and a transition

data.text: `useSprings` animates a list of values, `useTransition` manages mount and unmount, and `.to()` interpolates a raw value into a CSS string such as a percentage or a color. Springs can be chained so a follow-up animation starts when the first settles.

data.title: Interpolating a raw number
Springs vs duration-based easing
data.text: A CSS transition with a fixed duration is predictable and cheap; a spring looks more natural and reacts to interruption without a restart. The reason react-spring stands out is that it animates the values a CSS transition cannot — a canvas coordinate, an SVG path, an opacity driven by a gesture — through the same API.
